              Purpose:        This document clarifies the compliance requirements for grease interceptors (grease traps),




                                                                          BE
                              and serves to remind that such devices are also subject to the applicable requirements of
                              the Department of Environmental Protection (“DEP”).

             Related               PC      1003

           Subject(s):        Plumbing, grease trap; Plumbing, grease interceptor; Plumbing, kitchen
                                                 TS




Section PC 1003 of the New York City Plumbing Code provides the installation requirements for grease
interceptors (grease traps) to receive the drainage from fixtures and equipment with grease-laden waste located in
                                             C




food preparation areas, such as in restaurants, hotel kitchens, hospitals, school kitchens, bars, factory cafeterias or
                                       JE




restaurants, or clubs. In addition, due to the fact that the interceptors are a component of the waste discharge
system, the installation and sizing of grease interceptors are also regulated by the Rules of the DEP. The
additional installation and sizing requirements are found in 15 RCNY §19-11, “Best Management Practices (BMPs)
                            O




for Non-Residential Direct and Indirect Dischargers of Grease to the Public Sewer System”, as annexed on page 2
                          PR




through 4 of this document. Therefore, grease interceptors shall be sized to meet the sizing requirements in both
section PC 1003 and 15 RCNY §19-11.
                   R




For applications submitted on or after July 1, 2009, only those prefabricated grease interceptors that conform to
PDI G101, ASME A112.14.3 or ASME A112.14.4 shall be installed. Such interceptors shall not require Materials &
           FO




Equipment Acceptance (MEA) approvals from the Department of Buildings provided they are installed in
accordance with 15 RCNY §19-11, referenced standards in section PC 1003.3.4, and manufacturer’s instructions.
Such prefabricated grease interceptors shall be indicated on the approved construction plans as required by rules
 LY




of the Department of Buildings.

                              From Title 15 of the Rules of the City of New York
§19-11 Best Management Practices (BMPs) for Non-Residential Direct and Indirect Dischargers of
Grease to the Public Sewer System.




                                                                                                                               *
                                                                                                                  14
(a) Grease Interceptors shall be installed in waste lines which may receive grease from non-residential direct
and indirect dischargers, including, but not limited to, those leading from pot wash sinks, woks, soup or stock




                                                                                                                1-
kettles, food scrap sinks, scullery sinks, meat and/or poultry and/or fish preparation sinks, floor drains,




                                                                                                              -3
automatic dishwashers, scraper sinks or other similar plumbing fixtures in all restaurants, kitchens, cafeterias,
clubs, butcher shops, slaughterhouses, fish markets, supermarket food processing areas, delicatessens or other




                                                                                                       12
non-residential establishments where grease may be introduced into the drainage system. Sizing of grease
interceptors shall comply with the criteria specified in this section, including applicable Tables I and/or II.




                                                                                                 E
                                                                                         R
(b) All prefabricated grease interceptors shall be approved by the New York City Board of Standards &




                                                                                       FO
Appeals prior to July 10, 1991, approved by the New York City Department of Buildings Materials and
Equipment Acceptance Division prior to July 1, 2008, or shall conform to PDI G101, ASME A112.14.3 or
ASME A112.14.4 and shall be installed in accordance with the manufacturer’s instructions.

          If a premises contains fixtures listed in Table I and fixtures, vessels and/or receptacles listed in Table
II, all of which are tributary to the same grease interceptor, then the method for determining the minimum
grease interceptor retaining capacity in pounds shall be to separately calculate the retaining capacities for the




                                                                                                                    *
fixtures in Table I and the fixtures, vessels and/or receptacles in Table II. These retaining capacities shall then




                                                                                                       14
be added together to obtain the total minimum grease interceptor retaining capacity required for such premises.




                                                                                                     1-
        If the aggregate volumes listed in Tables I and II are exceeded, then a New York State Licensed
Professional Engineer or a New York State Registered Architect shall extrapolate the appropriate grease




                                                                                                   -3
interceptor sizing requirements.




                                                                                            12
(d) Vented flow control fittings shall be installed to insure that the flow capacity of the grease interceptor as




                                                                                      E
specified by the manufacturer is not exceeded. Flow-control valves and/or fittings that are manually
adjustable may not be used to limit flow to an interceptor.




                                                                           R
                                                                         FO
(e) Grease interceptors must have a retention capacity in pounds of at least twice the numerical flow-through
rate in gallons-per-minute.




                                                                  BE
(f) Grease interceptors shall remove an average of 90 percent or more of the grease or other extractable matter
in the wastewater.                                       D
                                                       LE
(g) The temperature of water entering a grease interceptor shall not exceed 180’F.
                                                  FI


(h) All grease interceptors must be readily accessible for inspection by duly authorized employees of the
Department.
                                           TS




(i) Grease interceptors for scraper sinks shall be sized in accordance with Table II, except that the minimum
                                       C




retaining capacity shall be at least 30 pounds. When determining the aggregate volume of all fixtures, vessels
and receptacles specified in Table II that may flow simultaneously through an interceptor, a minimum of 3,465
                                  JE




cubic inches per scraper sink shall be used.
                            O




(j) Dischargers from automatic dishwashers must be tributary to a grease interceptor. Whether connected
                          PR




separately or in conjunction with other fixtures, the total volume in gallons of each automatic dishwasher shall
be converted to cubic inches and added to the aggregate volume of Table II.
                   R




(k) Discharges from high-temperature sanitizer cycles of automatic dishwashers or from dedicated sanitization
           FO




compartments of sinks need not be tributary to a grease interceptor.

(l) Floor drains which may receive grease must be tributary to a grease interceptor. The size of such grease
 LY




interceptor shall be determined as follows:
N




          (1) For floor drains where grease maybe discharged during washdowns, Table I shall be used, and an
O




          additional 1,540 cubic inches per floor drain shall be added to the aggregate volume.

          (2) Grease interceptors for floor drains which receive discharges directly from fixtures, receptacles
          and/or vessels shall be sized in accordance with the grease interceptor sizing requirements for the
          fixtures, vessels and/or receptacles tributary to it.

          York State Licensed Professional Engineer or a New York State Registered Architect shall extrapolate
          the appropriate sizing requirements of the tributary grease interceptor based on (1) and/or (2) above.

based upon the total volume of all soup and stock kettles tributary to the grease interceptor even if the
discharges from these vessels are made to a floor drain or similar fixture.

                                                                                                   -3
interceptor, each wok shall be deemed to contribute 1,617 cubic inches to the aggregate volume of Table II.

(o) Discharges from the cleaning of kitchen hoods which may extract grease from cooking operations must be




                                                                                      E
made to receptacles or floor drains that are tributary to a grease interceptor. The sizing of the tributary grease

                                                                           R
automatic rinse cycles, the tributary grease interceptor must be sized to account for the peak flow from the




                                                                         FO

(p) Interceptors smaller than those described in Tables I and II may be used, but only if connected in parallel
to another interceptor(s), and the aggregate capacity of such interceptors must either equal or exceed the
interceptor capacity required by Tables I an/or II. For parallel connections, vented flow control fixtures must
                                                         D
be installed on each interceptor.
                                                       LE

(q) Grease interceptors shall be properly installed, maintained and operated to insure that the requirements of
                                                  FI


this section and other applicable sections of the regulations are met. This shall include routine cleaning and
grease removal from the interceptor as needed to insure the proper operation of the interceptors.
                                          TS




(r) New York State Licensed Professional Engineers and New York State Registered Architects may petition
                                      C




the Commissioner in writing for acceptance of an alternative pretreatment device, technology, equipment or
procedures varying from, but equivalent to, those listed in this section. Such a petition must contain detailed
                                 JE




documentation and calculations substantiating their equivalency. In no event shall any alternative
pretreatment device, technology, equipment or procedures be less stringent than the requirements of this
                            O




section.
                          PR




(s) Notwithstanding any other provision of this section, (1) existing grease interceptors shall conform to the
specific requirements of this section no later than one year after the effective date of this section, and (2)
                   R




grease interceptors installed after the effective date of this section pursuant to an application filed before such
           FO




effective date shall conform to the specific requirements of this section no later than 90 days after such
effective date.
 LY




(t) Notwithstanding anything contained in section 19-11 the Commissioner in his discretion may require any
grease interceptor to be installed at any time and to have a retention capacity equal to those listed in Tables I
N
